article_content: A device called the GT3D has been created in London, allowing control of computers and wheelchairs by tracking eye gaze. Originally costing £39.80, the price has dropped to around £20 due to cheaper camera costs. The GT3D, which uses video-game console cameras and glasses, works by calibrating where you look and interpreting these movements into cursor movements or potentially controlling complex systems. It could help people with disabilities such as Multiple Sclerosis, Parkinson's, and muscular dystrophy.

Con un costo original de £39.80, este ha reducido a £20 debido a la disminución de precios en las webcams de las consolas de juegos. El GT3D, que compone de dos micros, opera ajustando por dónde estás mirando para realizar movimientos en pantalla o controlar sistemas. Podría ofrecer alivio a personas con esclerosis, parkinson y distrofía muscular.

Mr Cameron appealed for cooperation in protecting national security.
